Question 5

Consider the function f(x)=x−x+13. Given that y=f(x) is invertible throughout its domain x≥1, determine (f−1)′(1).
(f−1)′(1)=
65​

EXPLANATION

To determine (f−1)′(1), we use the following formula: (f−1)′(1)=1f′(f−1(1))

First, we calculate the value of f−1(1). To do this, we solve the equation f−1(1)=x. This gives f−1(1)=xf(x)=1x−x+13=1x+13=x−1x+13=(x−1)2x+13=x2−2x+1x+1=3(x2−2x+1)x+1=3x2−6x+33x2−7x+2=0(3x−1)(x−2)=0x=13,2.

Since the domain of y=f(x) is x≥1, we have f−1(1)=2.

Now, we calculate f′(2), as follows: f(x)=x−x+13f′(x)=1−16x+13f′(2)=1−162+13f′(2)=1−161f′(2)=1−16f′(2)=56

Finally, we get (f−1)′(1)=1f′(f−1(1))=1f′(2)=1(56)=65.
